transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Cole (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (Celestia CTO), Priya Rao (ML Eng), Samir Khan (Infra), Jordan Lee (Product)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria and to model Celestia's inference workload (QPS, concurrency, token in/out distribution) - goal: define perf/benchmark plan, required infra, timelines. Customer leaning toward Dedicated but wants cost/latency tradeoffs for Hosted first.

Topics:
- Workload characterization: peak QPS, sustained QPS, concurrency patterns
- Token distribution (input length / output length) and sampling of traces
- Latency SLOs (p95/p99), batching, and KV cache expectations
- POC success criteria and timeline (benchmarks, accuracy checks, cost targets)
- Security / data retention notes for Private/Dedicated options

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we have about 45, 50 minutes, we'll try to run through the workload details and then align on next steps. Maya and Evan from my side will cover the perf plan.
[00:12] Alex: Yep thanks, Jared. Quick note, we only have Samir for the infra bits after 15:20 if we go deep.
[00:18] Maya: Great, quick goal - we want to size the POC so it's representative: identify peak QPS, concurrency, token distribution, then Redwood runs bench with those profiles.
[00:27] Priya: For context, our prod is a mix of synchronous chat-ish user requests and async batch enrichment. Peak real-time QPS is usually 120-150 sustained for ~20 minutes, but bursts hit ~320 for a few minutes during market opens.
[00:40] Samir: yeah and concurrency wise each request opens websocket clients, so concurrency is roughly equal to QPS for us during bursts, but for longer context the effective KV cache reuse drops.
[00:52] Evan: okay good, so two profiles: real-time low-latency at 120 sustained and burst at 300. Any long-tail async jobs we should include?
[01:05] Jordan: we have a nightly enrichment batch that spikes to ~600 simultaneous model calls but it's lower priority on latency, more throughput focused. So ideally POC covers both realtime and async.
[01:16] Maya: Perfect. On token distributions can you give rough means? Priya?
[01:22] Priya: Sure, user prompts average 120 tokens in, outputs are typically 80 tokens, though for summarization flows inputs go to 600 tokens and outputs ~150. Overall 70% of calls are <200 tokens, 20% 200-600, 10% >600.
[01:38] Jared: That's super helpful. For modeling we'll need a sample of traces - timestamps, input token count, response token count, and whether it's streaming.
[01:48] Alex: We can export logs, but a quick question - what's the overhead for streaming vs non-streaming on Redwood? Do you have numbers?
[01:55] Maya: Streaming adds a bit of latency overhead due to chunking and connection management, but it reduces time-to-first-byte for long outputs. In our internal tests with similar models, p95 increased by ~20-30ms for streaming path, but TTFB improved for >200 token outputs.
[02:10] Evan: Also depends on model - we can run the perf with both streaming enabled and disabled. For the POC we'll include the streaming profile since you use websockets.
[02:20] Samir: Security question - if we run Dedicated, can logs be kept in our VPC and KMS?
[02:25] Jared: Yes, Dedicated/Private supports customer-managed KMS and logs retained in your VPC. We'll share the SOC2/ISO docs after the call.
[02:33] Alex: Great. Back to sizing - what about batch sizes and quantization? We might want int8 for cost but need fidelity checks.
[02:41] Maya: We recommend starting with a float16/FP16 profile for quality baseline. Then test INT8/4-bit quantized variants for cost. We'll surface delta on quality with a small eval set. For batching we'll simulate both single-request mode and continuous batching with target batch windows (5-20ms) to meet your p95 targets.
[02:59] Priya: Our p95 SLO for user-facing flows is 450ms end-to-end right now, includes network and app layer - we want model latency p95 < 200ms ideally, p99 < 400ms.
[03:12] Evan: Noted - we'll aim model p95 < 180ms to give you buffer. For the burst scenario we'll show degradation curves as QPS increases.
[03:20] Jordan: Are you planning to use Redwood Dedicated for the POC? We are leaning that way for data residency.
[03:26] Jared: Customer choice; we can run the perf on Hosted first to show baseline, then mirror for Dedicated. Dedicated will be easier to hit consistent p95 at high QPS thanks to reserved GPU pools.
[03:36] Maya: We'll propose two benchmark runs: 1) Hosted baseline with autoscaled nodes to emulate your burst profile, 2) Dedicated run on pinned instance types so you can see tail latencies and cost.
[03:47] Alex: That sounds good. About metrics - we'll need token-level cost estimate, average token/sec, and per-1000-token cost.
[03:56] Jared: Yes we'll include cost per 1M tokens and a model selection comparison (latency vs cost) across 1-2 model sizes - e.g., 7B quantized vs 13B fp16 - depending on your accuracy needs.
[04:10] Priya: How long will the benchmark runs take? We need to factor in schedule.
[04:14] Evan: Typical perf run to stabilize stats is 30-60 minutes per profile, plus time to iterate. We recommend 1 hour for each of the three profiles (realtime baseline, burst, nightly batch), so ~3-4 hours total of running time spread across 1-2 days.
[04:29] Samir: For Dedicated sizing we need to know expected GPU types - will Redwood suggest instances?
[04:34] Maya: Yes we'll recommend GPU SKUs and memory configs in the benchmark proposal. For example, A10G or H100 depending on model and quantization. We'll include expected throughput numbers per GPU.
[04:44] Alex: On success criteria - what should we set as pass/fail?
[04:48] Jared: Good question. Proposed success criteria: 1) model p95 within target (<= 200ms) for realtime profile, 2) cost per 1M tokens below your threshold (TBD - Jordan?), 3) functionality/regression checks on a held-out eval set with <2% degradation vs baseline model.
[05:04] Jordan: For cost threshold, we were thinking < $X per 1M tokens, I'll confirm offline. But the latency and regression checks are the main gating factors.
[05:12] Priya: For the regression check, we'll provide an eval suite of ~500 prompts to validate output quality.
[05:19] Maya: Perfect. We'll run the eval before and after quantization.
[05:23] Evan: On instrumentation - please add request IDs to traces and include sample traces with KV cache warm/ cold patterns. We want to measure cache hit ratio impact on latency.
[05:34] Priya: We'll get that. Also note many requests reuse prefixes heavily during trading windows so cache is important.
[05:40] Jared: Ok to recap next steps: Maya to share benchmark spreadsheet and perf plan; Alex to upload traffic logs; Redwood to run Hosted perf then Dedicated; schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-12-08. Anything else?
[05:55] Alex: Could you also include an itemized cost comparison for Dedicated vs Hosted for the POC run?
[05:59] Jared: Yes, we'll include expected run cost and extrapolated monthly cost for your sustained load.
[06:04] Jordan: One more - any non-functional constraints around retention for logs? We need 7 year retention for audit events.
[06:11] Maya: For audit logs we can configure retention policies, and for Dedicated/Private you can push logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules. We'll note details in the security pack.
[06:20] Samir: Who's the contact for infra set up?
[06:23] Evan: I'll be the Redwood touchpoint for perf runs - I'll coordinate instance access and run windows.
[06:29] Alex: Great. That's all from me.
[06:32] Jared: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and pricing by tomorrow.
